newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Dollar buying pushes forint further below bid.
newsitem.headline: Dollar buying pushes forint further below bid.

text.p: Continued dollar buying depressed the forint on Wednesday, pushing it well below the National Bank of Hungary's resistance level (bid), dealers said.
The forint finished some 50 pips below the bid at 157.45/50 to one dollar, compared with 157.27/32 at the opening.
"The trend to dollar buying, which started yesterday, continued today and liquidity just dried up," said Ervin Csengeri of Inter-Europa Bank.
While some dealers said end-month import payments were one reason for the forint's fall, Csengeri suggested weaker forint interest rates also contributed.
"There's been a slide in forint interest rates recently and I think that's helped," he said.
Trade on the forex futures market of the Budapest Commodity Exchange fell to 3.17 billion forints from Tuesday's 11 billion.
The Swiss franc, which dominated Tuesday's bumper trade, and the yen were the most popular currencies.
